ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A = 50^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle OCB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\overset{\frown}{CB}=\overset{\frown}{CB}$ and $\angle A=50^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BOC=2\angle A=100^\circ$\\
Because $OB=OC$,\\
it is concluded that $\angle OCB=\angle OBC=\frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-\angle BOC)=\boxed{40^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a circle with points A, B, and C on the circumference, forming triangle ABC. Point O is shown inside the circle as the center, and segments OB and OC are drawn from O to points B and C, so OB and OC are radii. The chord/side BC is drawn at the bottom, and the requested angle is ∠OCB at point C. Reasoning: The given angle is ∠A = ∠BAC = 50°. This inscribed angle subtends arc BC. The central angle ∠BOC also subtends the same arc BC, so by the inscribed-angle theorem, ∠BOC = 2 × ∠BAC = 2 × 50° = 100°. Since OB and OC are both radii of the same circle, OB = OC, so triangle BOC is isosceles. Therefore ∠OBC = ∠OCB. The two base angles sum to 180° - 100° = 80°, so each is 80° ÷ 2 = 40°. Thus ∠OCB = 40°.

From the text, read that in triangle ABC, angle A equals 50°. Since angle BAC is an inscribed angle subtending arc BC, and central angle BOC subtends the same arc BC, use the inscribed-angle theorem to get angle BOC = 2 × 50° = 100°. Then in triangle BOC, use OB = OC because both are radii, so triangle BOC is isosceles. Therefore the base angles at B and C are equal, and each is (180° - 100°)/2 = 40°. Thus angle OCB is 40°.
